{0} The week runs from Monday to Sunday. The target never exceeds your weekly capacity with margin from the Load tab ({1} km a week).
Nevstřebaná zátěž z posledních dní proti: The load still unabsorbed from recent days against what you demonstrably handle in a week without trouble. Older days count only partly, by how much of them the body has already absorbed: a run 6 days ago about 30%, so it doesn't drop out of the calculation all at once. White tick = the ceiling (capacity with a 15% margin, by the week's readiness), where the load score starts to deduct. The week's target from Monday and today are on Training.
Dnešní kapacita = kolik si dnes můžete d: Today's capacity = how much you can afford today so that: (1) the load still unabsorbed from recent days stays within your weekly capacity — the same one the Load tab shows (capacity + 15% margin, by the week's readiness); older days count only partly, by how much of them the body has already absorbed, (2) this week (Monday to Sunday) stays within its target in the cycle (90 / 100 / 110 / 55%), (3) no single run goes over the single-run capacity, (4) the overall load (heart rate × time across all activities) stays under its ceiling. The strictest one applies — each channel shows which. When mechanics is over the threshold of 25, today shrinks further (volume −20%, intensity and descent halved); when load is over the threshold, a recovery week follows. That keeps both axes under the threshold.
Kapacita = co jste prokazatelně zvládli: Capacity = what you have demonstrably handled without trouble. Per week: the average week of the last 4 weeks, or 90% of the best week in 6 weeks (a week more than 30% above the ones before it doesn't count) — separately for volume, intensity (minutes in Z4+), descent, ascent and overall load (heart rate × time across all activities). Per run: the most demanding run of the last 30 days, for intensity the mean of the three hardest (one race or a hot day won't inflate the capacity). Runs followed within 3 days by pain ≥ 3/10 don't count. A jump of more than 30% over the capacity so far doesn't count at all for 14 days, and then fully only when a pain-free rating or check-in confirms it (otherwise half) — capacity grows only from what the body has demonstrably handled. Ceiling = capacity + margin (+15% per week, +10% per run), reduced by readiness. Above the ceiling load points build up. After a run the points are absorbed night by night: muscles and tendons with a half-life of about 3.5 nights, overall load and intensity faster after a good night and slower after a poor one (2–8 nights). A sharp jump also fades linearly until day 28. That's why the room under the ceiling also comes from the unabsorbed load: older days only partly (a run 6 days ago about 30%), today in full, so a long run doesn't drop out of the calculation all at once on the seventh day. Capacity and the ceiling roll from today, the week's target on Training runs Monday to Sunday.
The weekly target follows a 4-week cycle: week 1 at 90%, week 2 at 100%, week 3 at 110% of the reference week (the last full week before the previous recovery week), week 4 a recovery week — 55% of week 3. The app finds your place in the cycle from the last recovery week, otherwise from how demanding last week was against your norm. The week runs from Monday to Sunday. The target never exceeds your weekly capacity with margin (Load); with elevated load the recovery week comes earlier, before a race the taper. For the first 6 weeks of data the cycle doesn't run yet: the target is last week + 10%, the long run at most 10% longer than the longest in 30 days, and intensity and elevation don't block anything. After an injury you mark as healed come 3 weeks of graded return (50 / 75 / 90% of the week before the injury). The 3 + 1 pattern is common periodisation practice in endurance sports (Issurin 2010, Mujika 2018): load has to alternate with recovery (Meeusen 2013); the exact percentages are an established convention, which is why capacity and daily readiness keep watching it.
